Thesis.proseOnly: The thesis names the contract-vs-schedule split and the star-vs-ring 512x opening case; the primitive panels and the algorithm comparison carry it forward.

The Contract.teaches: The four group contracts as input -> operation -> output rows: AllReduce leaves Sigma on every rank, AllGather concatenates shards, ReduceScatter leaves one reduced shard per rank, AllToAll transposes chunks. The contract fixes the result, not the cost.
The Contract.source: fig-collective-primitives-overview: four panels, ranks 0-3, amber collective band, result tiles per primitive; Broadcast and Reduce as the two building blocks.

The Physics of a Moved Byte.proseOnly: The energy ladder (0.5/20/100/1,000 pJ) is the book's data-movement-hierarchy figure; the packet carries the n*-per-chunk regime point and the 100-alpha fusion arithmetic as prose.

Pricing the Schedule.teaches: The N=4 ring trace: 2(N-1)=6 steps split scatter-reduce (3) then all-gather (3); each rank sends ~2M total while rounds grow linearly. The byte floor vs the latency tax in one picture.
Pricing the Schedule.source: Ring AllReduce algorithm: scatter-reduce N-1 rounds then all-gather N-1 rounds; N=4 element-sum trace [10,26,18,34]; ring achieves 2(N-1)/N * M/beta bound (Patarasuk 2009).
Pricing the Schedule.alsoTeaches: crossover-map: modeled time vs message size on log axes; crossover near 1 MB at 256 GPUs on 200 Gbps; tree wins small, ring wins large; M* ~ N*alpha*beta/log2 N.

Topology-Aware Schedules.proseOnly: Hierarchical 3-phase (350 GB, 128x8, ~4-5x), torus 12-vs-30 rounds, rail-optimized 3->1 hops, and SHARP each have book figures (hierarchical-allreduce, torus-reduction, sharp-innetwork); the packet carries the numbers.

AllToAll and the MoE Exchange.proseOnly: Injection-bound arithmetic (8 x 262.144 KB at 6.5 us, ~38.2 us bound) and the 448-vs-672 hot-expert tail are mechanism prose; the contract panel already drew the transpose.

Trading Bits for Schedule.proseOnly: The compression table and the error-feedback trace (transmit 2, residual -0.4, true 1.6) are tabular content; the book's error-feedback margin figure covers the loop.

Hiding the Exchange.teaches: LogP split as two lanes: L=100us network transit hides beneath 500us compute, 2o=100us processor overhead stays exposed; DDP bucket chain where only the last bucket's transfer is exposed.
Hiding the Exchange.source: fig-comm-compute-overlap: compute lane (backward L4-L1 + o slices) vs network lane (AllReduce L4-L2 hidden, L1 exposed); LogP: 2o + max(compute, L) = 600us.

Calibration Before Diagnosis.proseOnly: Bus-bandwidth normalization (half of spec = ring traffic factor ~2) and the matched-measurement calibration contract are measurement prose, no new figure.

Fallacies and Pitfalls.proseOnly: Audit list of the claims the packet's numbers refute.
